intro: Sending me the best quality photo lets me create the best artwork for you. Whether you use a phone or a camera, these should help.

items.title: Patience and time
items.text: Don't rush it. Try over several days, and don't give up after one session.

items.title: Don't zoom
items.text: Walk closer instead. On a phone, zooming destroys quality. Try to fill the whole frame with your pet.

items.title: Use natural light
items.text: Nothing except professional lighting beats natural daylight. Avoid direct sunlight, which creates harsh shadows, but make sure there's plenty of light, even indoors.

items.title: Change your angle
items.text: Go high, go low, go left, go right, go eye level. Lie on the floor with them and see different views.

items.title: Let them see your camera
items.text: Let them sniff the phone or camera, especially if they seem uncomfortable, and turn your phone sounds off.

items.title: Treats always help
items.text: Not every animal enjoys having its photo taken. Have good light and be ready, then be quick. Say thank you afterwards with attention and treats.

items.title: Good timing helps
items.text: Catch them when they're lazy or lying down. Set up first, then get close gently so you don't give them a fright.

items.title: Consider the surroundings
items.text: A white dog on a white blanket, or a black dog on a black one, disappears into the background. Contrast between pet and background gives the best results.

items.title: Some no-no's
items.text: No flash, no evening or night photos, and no blur. If you send me a blurry photo, I'll draw a blurry drawing.

items.title: Sounds
items.text: Try interesting (not loud) sounds to catch their interest. This is how I get my tilted-head shots.

items.title: Take loads of photos
items.text: Snap away on many different days. The more you take, the easier it gets, and the more you'll have to choose from and to keep once they're gone.

items.title: Be nice
items.text: Never shout or make it stressful. They'll remember that photos are a bad thing. The calmer and more fun it is for your pet, the better.

items.title: Ask for help
items.text: Know someone who loves taking selfies or photographing their food? Ask them to help, and give them treats to hand out.

signoffText: Most importantly, enjoy the time with your fur babies. Take a look at their cute noses and all the texture on them. I love creatures' little noses.
